title: Air Fryer Tortilla de Patatas
description: One small Spanish tortilla with no flipping. A side for salmon, or a light dinner with a salad. Not yet cooked, so report back and I will adjust the timings.

source.name: Spanish source, air fryer timings sourced

confidence.note: Spanish source, air fryer timings sourced. Not yet cooked, so report back and I will adjust the timings.

items.note: Approx. 2 eschalots or ½ brown onion
Plus extra to grease the tin

steps.text: Toss the potatoes ({{potatoes}}) with most of the olive oil ({{oil}}) and most of the salt ({{salt}}).
Air fry the potatoes directly in the basket at 180°C for 9 minutes, shaking halfway.
Toss the eschalots or onion ({{eschalots}}) in the remaining oil, add to the basket, shake, and cook a further 8 minutes, until the potatoes are tender and the onion is soft.
Beat the eggs ({{eggs}}) with the remaining salt. Grease a 15–18cm tin or silicone liner, tip in the potatoes and onion, and pour over the egg, pressing the potatoes down so they are covered.
Place the tin in the basket, leaving space around it, and cook at 160°C for 17 minutes.
Increase to 180°C for 5 minutes to set the centre and colour the top. A knife in the centre should come out without runny egg.
Rest in the tin 5 minutes, then run a knife around the edge and turn out. Serve warm or at room temperature.

notes.title: Confidence
notes.text: Quantities are halved from Diez Minutos (Spain). Air fryer temperatures and times are from Recipe This. Estimated: the salt, oil and eschalot weight, and the split of the 17-minute potato cook into 9 plus 8 minutes so the eschalots do not scorch.

notes.title: Silicone liner
notes.text: Use it for the egg stage only. Put it in the basket before filling. A 20cm liner gives a thinner tortilla, so start checking the centre at 12–15 minutes at 160°C (estimate). Expect a paler base than a metal tin.

notes.title: Potato stage
notes.text: Straight in the basket, not the liner. The liner blocks airflow and the slices steam unevenly. If you do use it to save washing up, shake more often and allow a few extra minutes.

notes.title: Shallots on the label
notes.text: In Queensland, shallots often means spring onions. Those cook too fast to fry with the potatoes, so stir them through the egg instead.

notes.title: Full batch
notes.text: Use the servings control for 4. That needs two tins cooked one after the other, unless one larger tin fits the basket with room for air.

notes.title: Pan version
notes.text: The Diez Minutos original: 1kg potatoes and 1 onion fried in 150ml extra virgin olive oil, drained, split between two bowls of 4 beaten eggs each, then cooked as two tortillas in a 16–18cm pan and flipped with a plate. The source ingredient list says 7 eggs but the method uses 8.

notes.title: Thermomix
notes.text: Not much use here. It cannot brown or set the tortilla. Slicing the onion is the only real time-saver.
